story.value: The name lutetium comes from Lutetia, the ancient name for the city of Paris.
The discovery of lutetium is credited to the French chemist Georges Urbain in 1907.
Carl Auer von Welsbach had named the element cassiopeium, after the constellation Cassiopeia.

uses.value: Lutetium has no large scale practical uses.
Stable forms of lutetium can be used as catalysts in processes such as hydrogenation and polymerization.
Almost no other commercial uses have been found for lutetium yet.
